alternatives_considered.approach: Fix only the ingest path and leave computeFunnel summing whatever is stored

work_order.approach: Keep the v1 plan's tenant-wide aggregation convention exactly as built — it is proven by all six passing ACs — and close the two money-integrity holes with enforcement at two layers. Ingest layer: normaliseGrowthEvent rejects spend.observed whose assembled amount_micros is not positive (covers both the body.value path and the pre-normalised payload.amount_micros path) with stable code NON_POSITIVE_SPEND, so zero and negative spend never reach storage; the POST route additionally enforces one currency per tenant, seeding a new tenant's currency from its first spend event (default INR otherwise, preserving seed and existing behaviour) and rejecting later spend in any other currency with stable code CURRENCY_MISMATCH, reusing the money.js code for mixing currencies. Read layer (defence in depth for append-only legacy rows that ingest guards can never remove): computeFunnel gains an optional second parameter for the tenant currency, always skips non-positive spend amounts, and — only when the currency is supplied — skips spend rows carrying an explicitly different currency, so pre-existing bad rows stop corrupting metrics without changing single-argument call behaviour relied on by existing tests. No dashboard change: once the funnel is single-currency and positive, the existing formatMoney rendering is correct. Validation stays before tenant auto-creation, so every 4xx still writes nothing.
assumptions: Single-currency-per-tenant is acceptable for single-operator v1; genuine multi-currency operation needs an FX epic and is out of scope

A new tenant's first spend event defines its currency; a tenant first created by a non-spend event keeps the INR default, so a later foreign-currency spend is a 400 and the operator uses a fresh tenant id

files.change: In normaliseGrowthEvent, after the payload is assembled: when event_name is spend.observed and payload.amount_micros is present, require it to be a positive safe integer, else return ok:false with measurementError code NON_POSITIVE_SPEND (message naming the received value). This single check covers both the body.value path and the pre-normalised payload.amount_micros path, and it runs before tenant auto-creation so rejected spend writes nothing. In computeFunnel, add an optional second parameter (tenant currency string): always skip spend.observed rows whose amount_micros is not a positive safe integer, and when the currency argument is supplied also skip spend rows whose payload.currency is present and differs from it (rows with no currency are treated as tenant-currency for v1 leniency). Single-argument calls keep today's behaviour on positive rows, so existing funnel tests are unaffected.
files.why: Ingest rejects non-positive spend with a stable code; the funnel can never invert or zero CPL even over append-only legacy bad rows

files.change: In the POST /v1/events handler, after validation and before append: resolve the tenant row; when the event is spend.observed with a currency, if the tenant row exists and its currency differs, return 400 CURRENCY_MISMATCH with no write; when auto-creating an unknown tenant, seed its currency from the spend event's currency when present, else 'INR' as today. In the GET /v1/metrics handler, pass the tenant row's currency (default 'INR' when the tenant row is absent) as the second argument to computeFunnel so foreign-currency legacy rows are excluded from spend_micros and qualified_cpl_micros.

work_order.root_cause: Two money-integrity checks the v1 plan never specified, both in the spend path. BUG-1: normaliseGrowthEvent (src/domain/measurement.js) validates money shape — Number.isSafeInteger — but never sign, so spend.observed with value <= 0 normalises ok:true and computeFunnel sums it, letting negative spend invert qualified_cpl_micros and paired +X/-X rows cancel real spend to zero. BUG-2: per-event currency is validated as a known ISO code but never compared to the tenant's unit of account (tenants.currency, default INR on auto-create), and computeFunnel adds payload.amount_micros without inspecting payload.currency — bypassing the CURRENCY_MISMATCH guard that src/domain/money.js enforces — so INR+USD micros sum into a CPL denominated in no real currency that the dashboard then mislabels with the tenant currency string.

cases: normaliseGrowthEvent rejects spend.observed with a negative value with code NON_POSITIVE_SPEND (the QA BUG-1 repro)
normaliseGrowthEvent rejects spend.observed with value 0 with code NON_POSITIVE_SPEND
normaliseGrowthEvent rejects a pre-normalised negative payload.amount_micros on spend.observed without body.value
normaliseGrowthEvent still accepts a positive spend.observed and non-spend events are unaffected by the positivity rule
computeFunnel skips non-positive spend rows from legacy batches so paired +X/-X rows can no longer cancel to zero
computeFunnel with a tenant-currency argument excludes explicitly foreign-currency spend rows (the QA BUG-2 repro) while single-argument calls keep today's behaviour on positive rows
POST spend.observed with a negative value returns 400 NON_POSITIVE_SPEND with {code,message} and no stack, creates no tenant row, and leaves metrics absent
POST spend.observed with value 0 returns 400 NON_POSITIVE_SPEND
POST spend.observed in a currency different from the existing tenant's currency returns 400 CURRENCY_MISMATCH with unchanged metrics (the QA BUG-2 repro: USD spend against an INR tenant)
POSTing a USD-first journey to a fresh tenant auto-creates the tenant in USD and resolves CPL in USD
full 10-event INR journey on an isolated tenant still resolves via GET /v1/metrics to qualified_cpl_micros 2400000000 with volume 3 (no regression on AC-1)

work_order.understanding: The v1 plan's core diagnosis was NOT wrong, and this is not a re-roll of a mistaken premise: its pinned tenant-wide aggregation convention is proven — all six acceptance criteria pass against the live preview and CI is green. What the previous attempt got wrong was an omission, not a misdiagnosis: the plan specified money shape (safe-integer micros, known ISO currency code) but never specified money integrity — sign or unit of account — so the implementer faithfully built exactly what was asked and QA's two major bugs walked through holes the work order left open. BUG-1: negative and zero spend.observed ingests with 202 and inverts (or cancels to zero) the tenant's qualified CPL. BUG-2: INR and USD micros sum into a CPL denominated in no real currency that the dashboard mislabels. Neither bug contradicts the tenant-wide rule; both corrupt its inputs. The fix therefore keeps the convention untouched and adds two-layer enforcement (reject at ingest with stable codes NON_POSITIVE_SPEND and CURRENCY_MISMATCH, plus a read-side guard in computeFunnel for append-only legacy rows), with regression tests and two new acceptance criteria AC-7/AC-8 so QA holds the contract on every future run.
